name: SN74LVC1G125DBVR
title: SN74LVC1G125: single bus buffer gate, 3-state output, 1.65 V to 5.5 V
summary: One non-inverting buffer in the LVC family whose output turns off (high impedance) when the active-low OE input is high. It runs from 1.65 V to 5.5 V, its inputs take 5.5 V at any supply, and Y sources or sinks 24 mA at 3 V and 32 mA at 4.5 V. Ioff turns the output off with the supply removed, for live insertion and partial power-down. Offered in SOT-23 (DBV), SC70 (DCK), SOT-5X3 (DRL), SON (DRY, DSF), X2SON (DPW) and DSBGA (YZP); SN74LVC1G125DBVR is the SOT-23 part on a 3000-piece reel.
key_figures: 1.65 V to 5.5 V (data retention to 1.5 V)

circuits.title: Typical application: 3.3 V logic up to 5 V logic
circuits.description: Up-translation: U1 sits on the regulated 5 V rail, so Y swings rail to rail at 5 V into a 5 V controller, logic or LED load, while A is driven from a controller on a 3.3 V rail. A separate buffer drives OE; holding it low keeps the path enabled. C1 decouples VCC to ground next to U1.

operation.text: One non-inverting buffer with a 3-state output. With OE low, Y follows A; with OE high, Y is off whatever A does.
For Y to stay off while the supply ramps up or down, OE is pulled up to VCC with a resistor. How low that resistor can go is set by how much current the circuit driving OE can sink.

The output drives high, drives low, or floats, and sinks about as much current as it sources. Its edges are fast into light loads, so trace routing and load can produce ringing. It can deliver more current than it survives: keep it within the absolute maximum current and thermal limits. Off, it only leaks (IOZ) and leaves the line voltage to the rest of the circuit; a pull-up or pull-down, typically 10 kΩ, holds a known level. An unused output may be left open; never tie an output straight to VCC or ground, and never join push-pull outputs that can disagree.

With VCC at 0 V an internal circuit turns the output off, so it neither sources nor sinks current whatever the inputs do; leakage is the Ioff figure, ±10 µA at 5.5 V. This supports live insertion, partial power-down and back-drive protection.

Inputs are high impedance, a resistance in parallel with CI. Edges must meet the rise/fall-rate limit; slow edges raise supply current, can make the part oscillate and shorten its life. No input may float: tie an unused one to VCC or GND, and give an input that is not always driven a pull-up (default high) or pull-down (default low), 10 kΩ being the usual value. An input held at VCC - 0.6 V instead of a rail costs up to 500 µA of extra supply current.

Input and output each have only a clamp diode to ground (IIK, IOK); there is no diode to VCC on the inputs. Inputs therefore accept up to 5.5 V above a lower VCC, which provides down translation to VCC. The negative voltage limits may be exceeded if the clamp currents stay within rating; the 6.5 V input maximum may never be exceeded.

The input thresholds are low enough for TTL levels (VIL 0.8 V, VIH 2 V), so the buffer can take a 3.3 V signal up to 5 V. The output drive is modest and its edges slow enough to limit overshoot and undershoot on bus lines prone to ringing.

All specifications hold for a total load capacitance up to 50 pF. A larger capacitance may be driven through a series resistor between Y and the load to limit current. Keep traces to the receiver short to hold the load capacitance down. Most CMOS inputs present megohms, far above the minimum load resistance.

Any supply within the recommended range works; it must source and the ground must sink the total output current plus ICC and the switching transients, within the ±100 mA VCC/GND rating. Decouple VCC with 0.1 µF placed close to both VCC and GND; 0.1 µF and 1 µF in parallel cover a wider band of noise.

Bypass capacitor next to the supply pin, with a short ground return, wide traces, and on the same board side as the part where possible. Signal traces 8 mil to 12 mil wide and shorter than 12 cm, without 90° corners, over an unbroken ground plane with ground flood around them; parallel traces at least three dielectric thicknesses apart. Beyond 12 cm: controlled impedance, a 22 Ω series damping resistor at the driver, and no branches, each branch getting its own buffer.
Self-heating is seldom a concern in a logic gate; the junction temperature limit still applies.
The part can be damaged by electrostatic discharge, from slight parameter shifts to outright failure; handle it with ESD precautions.
SN74LVC1G125-Q1 is an AEC-Q100 automotive version and SN74LVC1G125-EP an enhanced-product version for defense, aerospace and medical use.

All active orderable parts with a listed rating are MSL 1 at 260 °C peak reflow. DBV follows JEDEC MO-178 and DCK MO-203 (its lead width is outside JEDEC); mold flash and gate burrs are excluded from body dimensions and may add up to 0.25 mm per side on DBV and DCK and 0.15 mm on DRL. The DBV and DCK support pin may differ or be absent. DRL follows MO-293 variation UAAD-1 and DSF MO-287 variation X2AAF. DPW occupies 0.64 mm² at 0.5 mm pitch, its GND being the centre pad. YEA is the tin-lead version of the bare-die package and YZA the lead-free one, both to MO-211 variation EA; YEP is tin-lead, with YZP as its lead-free counterpart.
